raw.details:
Clarification Note: The Round 1 shortlisting approach has been revised. Participants will now be evaluated based on their GitHub profile, LinkedIn profile, and best project built so far. Problem statements will be released on the day of the on-campus hackathon. Please refer to the updated stage descriptions for details.

Registration Note: All registrations will be completed exclusively through our official website. Please use the link below to register.

“Exploit the Code. Forge the Future.”

Description:

The Devforge is a 24-hour coding marathon where teams of 2–4 developers brainstorm, design, and build innovative solutions to real-world problems under pressure. Collaborate with your squad, tackle challenges, and race against the clock as you turn bold ideas from concept into working solutions — a true test of creativity, problem-solving, teamwork, and technical skill.

Eligibility:

  • Open to college students across India
  • Inter-college teams are allowed
  • Inter-specialization teams are allowed
  • Team size must be between 2 to 4 members

Rules & Regulations:

  • Participants must bring their own laptops, chargers, and devices.
  • Internet access will be provided.
  • Pre-built projects are not allowed. All code must be written during the hackathon (libraries/frameworks permitted).
  • Teams must present a working prototype at the end.
  • Participants are required to stay on campus for the duration of the hackathon(Food will be provided in the campus)
  • Teams must adhere to all guidelines and submission formats
  • The judges’ decision will be final.
  • Code Freeze: Submission deadline for Day 1 code freeze (09:00 AM) is absolute; no further commits will be considered for Round 2 evaluation.

Registration Process:

Note:

  • The hackathon will consist of 2 rounds.

  • Round 1 will involve application and shortlisting based on participants' technical profiles and past projects.

  • Shortlisted teams will advance to the 24-hour offline hackathon at the Scaler School of Technology (SST) campus.

  • Problem statements will be revealed on the day of the event.

  • Selected teams will advance to the final evaluation round for live presentations and product demonstrations.

Round 1:

  • Online profile and project-based shortlisting.

    • Submit your GitHub profile, LinkedIn profile, and a link to the best project you have built so far per member.
    • Ensure all submitted links are accessible and showcase your technical capabilities and past work.
    • Teams will be evaluated based on their technical skills, project quality, implementation capabilities, and problem-solving ability.
    • Shortlisted teams will be notified via their registered email address and invited to participate in the on-campus hackathon.

Round 2 (Final Round):

  • 24 hours on campus, building and presenting functional prototypes.

    • Problem statements will be revealed on the day of the event.
    • Build, test, and iterate on a functional prototype during the 24-hour, on-campus hackathon, with mentorship support for system design, debugging, and development.
    • Final deliverables include a working prototype and GitHub repository submission, with an optional demo and presentation.
    • Based on their submissions, selected teams will advance to the final evaluation round to present their solutions to the judges.
    • Evaluation will be based on innovation, technical complexity, feasibility, impact, and presentation. Final rankings and prize winners will be determined based on the evaluation.
    Disqualification Criteria:
  • Plagiarism or code copying.
  • Submitting incomplete or non-functional prototypes.
  • Submitting pre-existing projects, cloning repositories without substantial original contribution, or fabricating Git history.
  • Presenting mockups or pre-rendered videos as live working software.
  • Misconduct, harassment, damage to venue facilities, or disrupting the event.

Step-by-Step Registration & Submission Guide:

  • Step 1 (Register Team): Register your team leader on our official website with this link : THE DEVFORGE and send invitation links to 1–3 team members (total team size: 2–4).
  • Step 2: Please provide all the requested details as instructed.

Participant Advisory (What to Pack for Offline Rounds)

  • Hardware & Electronics: Laptops, power adapters, extension cords, mouse/mousepads, and mobile hotspots (backup connectivity).
  • Comfort Items: Light jacket or hoodie (halls are air-conditioned overnight), neck pillow, or compact travel blanket.
  • Personal Essentials: Personal toiletries, medication, hygiene kit, and reusable water bottle.
